extracted.intended_audience: readers, instructors, and students using Stein & Shakarchi's 'Fourier Analysis' textbook; mathematicians checking errata
extracted.subtask_description: Errata listing corrections to formulas, hypotheses, parametrizations, variable names, domains, and sign conventions in the Stein & Shakarchi textbook 'Fourier Analysis'. Intended to correct and clarify the printed mathematical statements and derivations.

rubrics_metrics.name: p.90 Exercise 10 — correct time variable in E(t)
rubrics_metrics.description: The correct formula for E(t) should refer to τ and not T: E(t) = 1/2 ρ_0 ∫ ... (∂u/∂t) dx + 1/2 τ_0 ∫ ... (∂u/∂x) dx.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the variable τ (tau) consistently in the displayed energy formula for E(t) rather than T. Ensure the integrals and their integrands use the intended time/parameter symbol to avoid confusion or incorrect interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: p.125 Problem 1* — convexity assumption and parametrization
rubrics_metrics.description: One must assume (for part (b)) that Γ is also convex. Moreover, in the argument to establish part (b) one must pick a parametrization γ so that for each t ∈ [−π, π] the tangent to the curve makes an angle t with the y-axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state needed geometric hypotheses (Γ is convex) when formulating parts of problems/theorems. When choosing a parametrization, impose the orientation/tangent-angle condition required by the argument (here: tangent angle equals t with the y-axis for t ∈ [−π,π]).

rubrics_metrics.name: p.136–137 — correct difference quotient/decomposition for Fourier transform
rubrics_metrics.description: The last formula on page 136 should read: (ˆf(ξ+h) − ˆf(ξ))/h − (−2πix f)^(ξ) = ∫_{−∞}^{∞} f(x)e^{−2πixξ} (e^{−2πixh} − 1)/h dx + 2πix ∫_{−∞}^{∞} f(x)e^{−2πixξ} dx. Also, the estimate on line 7 from the top of page 137 should start with (ˆf(ξ+h) − ˆf(ξ))/h − (−2πix f)^(ξ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relating difference quotients of the Fourier transform to multiplication by −2πix, write the decomposition and limits precisely so that the error term is the integral with (e^{−2πixh}−1)/h. Ensure subsequent estimates begin from the correct expression. This preserves the correct identification of the derivative of the transform and the remainder term.

rubrics_metrics.name: p.155 — consistent use of dummy variable (replace ϑ(s) by ϑ(t))
rubrics_metrics.description: In the last equation of the page, ϑ(s) should be replaced by ϑ(t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistent variable names in displayed equations; replace mistakenly used dummy variables so that equations match surrounding text and intended dependencies (here, use ϑ(t) rather than ϑ(s)).

rubrics_metrics.name: p.158 Theorem 4.1 — correct formula/constants for A2 = |A|^2
rubrics_metrics.description: The displayed formula A2 = |A|^2 = 2B/π (as printed) should be replaced by the corrected expression (erratum indicates the printed constant/formula is incorrect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure constants and algebraic relationships stated in theorem statements and proofs are numerically and symbolically correct; correct any misprinted coefficients or equalities in theorems to match the intended mathematical result.

rubrics_metrics.name: p.166 Exercise 19(b) — state domain of validity
rubrics_metrics.description: The formulas are valid for 0 < t < 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always state the domain/range of parameters for which formulas or identities hold. Add the missing restriction 0 < t < 1 to avoid misuse of the formulas outside their valid range.

rubrics_metrics.name: p.217 Problem 7(d) — correct sign conventions and boundary-limit formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: The signs on the right hand side of the formulas are incorrect as printed. The two formulas should read: (−Δ)^{1/2} f(x) = − lim_{y→0} ∂u/∂y (x,y), and (−Δ)^{k/2} f(x) = (−1)^k lim_{y→0} ∂^k u/∂y^k (x,y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify sign conventions for fractional Laplacians/derivative operators and their representation via boundary limits of harmonic extensions. Correctly include overall sign factors (including (−1)^k) and the limiting procedure as y→0 to match the operator definitions.
